text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Moi gives his word to church that government will review administrative and legislative framework to ensure free and fair elections.
- Hundreds of Kenya Polytechnic students take to streets for second day demanding release of 14 colleagues arrested after riots on Monday.
- Retired Judge William Mbaya says judiciary's independence has been reduced by consistent interference of executive arm of government.
- Islamic preacher Sheikh Khalid Balala orders Moslems to surrender voter registration cards to him so that he may burn them on Friday.
- Kenyans residing in Stockholm have organised two-hour pro-reform demonstration to be held at Kenyan Embassy on Friday.
- Opposition Democratic Party Chairman Mwai Kibaki vows he will not step down in race for presidential candidate from party.
- Balala accused of engaging in non-Islamic activities that have seriously compromised the faith.
- Japanese ambassador to Kenya Shinsuke Horiuchi says normal economic activities in country could be adversely affected by political tension.
- A leading agitator for constitutional reforms, Kivutha Kibwana, says leaders advocating boycott and disruption of general election should abandon idea.
